bull_bear.body: The company has a robust financial position, with a strong balance sheet and a CRISIL AA/Stable rating.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: The company faces risks related to intense competition, volatility in raw material prices, and regulatory changes.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The company's strong relationships with its customers and suppliers are a key competitive advantage.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet position given as Long term debt (gross) INR 508 cr and Net INR 93 cr, with Free Cash of INR 415 cr described as "8% of revenue" (the deck gives both figures on the same line without reconciling them).
- The "100% IAC Merger" is justified in capital-allocation terms: "To boost free cash, better leverage for future inorganic steps."
- Inorganic growth is an explicit plank - past revenue-to-target charts are labelled "Organic + Inorganic" and "Future Acquisitions" is listed among the accelerated-growth drivers.
- Value-creation targets are set at 20% EBITDA margin and 20% ROCE under the FY26-FY31 vision; the deck states no dividend policy, payout ratio or buyback.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: The company's automotive lighting segment accounts for the majority of its revenue, followed by the auto components segment.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Framed as "8 Decades of Group Legacy" and "2 Decades of Lumax Auto Technologies", built through "Growth Through Partnerships, Product Diversification & Strategic Acquisition".
- The 20-year transformation table contrasts 2005 with 2026: revenue Rs. 100 Cr to Rs. 4,870 Cr; product lines 1 (Lighting) to "Diverse - 13+ Advanced plastics, Interior Solutions, Metallics, Lighting, Aftermarket, Sensors, Electronics, Telematics & alternate fuels"; plants 1 to 28; engineering strength <10 ("Reverse engineering & Built to print") to >500 ("Innovation & IPR focused"); JVs/alliances NIL to 7; sector focus "2W only" to a "Healthy mix of PV/2W/CV".
- Stated ambition is to move from Tier-1 to Tier-0.5 system integrator under the mid-term theme "BRIDGE: Bold Roadmap Integrating Diverse Growth Engines", with the framing "What got us here will not take us there!".
- JV/alliance partner set named across eras: SL Corporation (Korea, at Lumax Industries level), Cornaglia (Italy), Mannoh Industrial (Japan), FAE (Spain), Ituran (Israel), Yokowo (Japan) and Alps Alpine (Japan).
- Q1FY27 revenue mix as disclosed - product-wise: Advance Plastics 56%, Structures & Control Systems 16%, Aftermarket 8%, Alternate Fuels 8%, Mechatronics 6%, Others 6%; segment-wise: PV 52%, 2/3W 27%, Aftermarket 8%, CV 8%, Others 5%; customer-wise: M&M 30%, Bajaj 16%, MSIL 9%, Aftermarket 8%, LIL 6%, TATA 6%, HMSI 5%, Others (Misc) 20%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisitions] The 2023-2026 era records acquisition of a 60% stake in Greenfuel Energy Solutions, completion of the merger of IAC India (described elsewhere as "100% acquisition of IAC India"), and the opening of the SHIFT tech centre plus the Japan satellite and China representative offices.
- [JV ownership] Disclosed shareholdings: Mannoh 55%, Cornaglia 50%, Alps Alpine 50%, Ituran 50%, Yokowo 50%, FAE 100%, Greenfuel Energy 60%.
- [Subsidiary order books] Greenfuel Rs. 200 crores, Alps Alpine Rs. 154 Crores, Mannoh Rs. 94 crores, Yokowo Rs. 85 crores, Cornaglia Rs. 49 crores, Ituran Rs. 23 Crores, FAE Rs. 6 Crores.
- [Customer concentration by entity] Key customers named per JV: Mannoh (MSIL, M&M, Toyota, TATA, HCIL, Daimler), Cornaglia (Tata, Toyota, Volkswagen, M&M, MG), Alps Alpine (MSIL, HMSI), Ituran (Daimler), Yokowo (M&M, HCIL, Toyota), FAE (REML, M&M), Greenfuel (MSIL, Tata, SML, VECV).
- [Recognition] Seventh consecutive year of LACP Awards recognition (ranked #72 globally, Platinum - Annual Report, Gold - Integrated Report), seven consecutive years of ICQCC recognition, JIPM-TPM Excellence Award March 2026 for the Metallics Division at Kuruli, and GreenPro Ecolabel Certification for four products each from the LATL Chakan and Pantnagar plants.

deepdive.thesis: Lumax Auto Technologies Limited is a leading manufacturer of automotive lighting and components, with a strong presence in the Indian market and a growing export business. The company has a diversified product portfolio and a robust financial position, with a CRISIL AA/Stable rating. However, the company faces intense competition and volatility in raw material prices.

open.item: Board recommended a dividend of ₹5.50 per equity share (275% of face value) for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.
Setting up first China office, expected operational by January 2026, for sourcing, tooling, and technology scouting.
Effective tax rate expected to hold at 25-26% for full year FY26.
Aftermarket segment growth expected to accelerate to 15-20% in H2 FY26, with October already at 20%.
Revised full-year FY26 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 25% from earlier 20%.
Maintain full-year FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin guidance of 14% to 15%.
Full-year FY26 capex guidance maintained at INR 200-220 crore.
IAC India full-year FY26 revenue expected around INR 1,450 crore, ~20% growth.
Greenfuel Energy Solutions full-year FY26 revenue target INR 350-400 crore.
Mega mechatronics plant at Manesar under commissioning; phase-wise move of 4 JVs starting March/April 2026.

Commissioning a Mega Mechatronics Plant at Manesar, slated for launch by FY 2026-27, consolidating four JVs (Lumax Yokowo, Lumax Alps Alpine, Lumax Ituran, Lumax FAE) with captive PCB SMT lines, clean rooms and sensor management control rooms.
Lumax Yokowo target EBITDA margin of 13-15% by FY27.
Mechatronics division target INR 500+ crore revenue by FY28.
Target clean mobility (EV/alternate fuels) to reach 40% of total LATL portfolio by FY28.
Robust order book of INR 1,357 crore with visibility across next 3 fiscal years.
Order book phasing: ~7% in FY26, 35% in FY27, 48% in FY28, 10% in FY29.
Alps Alpine JV targeting >INR 500 crore revenue by FY30.
Aspires to more than double current revenue base to upwards of ₹10,000 Crore by FY 2030-31, via organic growth and inorganic opportunities.
Mid-term BRIDGE plan (FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31) targets 20%+ revenue CAGR, driven by new product segments and strategic acquisitions.
Mid-term BRIDGE plan targets 20%+ Return on Capital Employed (ROCE), reflecting disciplined capital allocation.
